texts.preamble: M/S. Acalmar Oils Fats Ltd., E.G.Dist. ... vs Food Inspector, Anantahpur Ano on 24 November, 2020 Author: B.Krishna Mohan Bench: B.Krishna Mohan Hon'Ble Sri Justice B.Krishna Mohan Criminal Petition No. 3099 Of 2015 Order:
texts.facts: This criminal petition arises against the Proceedings in CC No.508 of 2007 on the file of the Court of IV Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Dharmavaram, against the Petitioners/A-3 and A-2, for the alleged violation of Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(m) punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 ( for short "the Act"). The petitioners are shown as A-3 and A-2 and the 2nd respondent herein is shown as A-1 in CC No.508 of 2007 on the file of the Court of IV Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Dharmavaram. The allegations of the complaint disclose that on 31.07.2006 at about 1.00 p.m. the 1st respondent along with his staff had inspected 'Mysore Bakery', at which time, the 2nd respondent/A-1 was present at the shop. During the course of inspection, the 1st respondent found 2 cartons and each carton containing 15 kgs. box of 'New Aadhar Bake Well Interesterfied Vegetable Oil' along with sweets, mixure etc., which were meant for sale for human consumption. On 01.08.2006 the 1st respondent after collecting the samples, divided the said vegetable oil into three parts and sent one part to the Public Analyst, State Food Laboratory, Hyderabad, and entrusted the remaining two parts to the local authorities of Anantapur for preservation. Subsequently, the Public Analyst sent the report dated 07.09.2006 opining that the sample does not confirm to the standards of Red Units in respect of Sesame Oil and reported that the product is adulterated as per Section 2(ia) (m) of the Act, 1954. Basing upon the same, the 1st respondent gave complaint on 28.08.2007 against the petitioners/A-3 and A-2 and the 2nd respondent/A-1 for the offences stated above. After filing the charge sheet, the learned IV Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Dharmavaram, took cognizance of the case and numbered the case as CC No.508 of 2017 and issued notices to the accused.
texts.arguments: It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the proceedings in the above CC cannot be continued since Section 13(2) of the Act contemplates that ten days time would be there for the petitioners to seek for sending the products for further analysis to the Central Food M/S.
